archetype.name: Improviser (spot-start backup)
archetype.definition: A second-year backup who holds the ball, hunts the big play and lives with the sacks that come with it, and whose value right now comes in occasional spot duty behind Deshaun Watson.

report.headline: One loud spot start, built on three deep balls and a pile of sacks
report.take:
Shedeur Sanders is the Browns' QB2. Watson started eight of the first ten weeks, Sanders got the Week 9 start in New Orleans, and Watson was back under center in Week 10. Nearly everything in his 2026 line comes from that one afternoon: 19 of 31 for 297 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, five sacks and +4.3 passing EPA in a one-point loss. The other two appearances were one-snap and 6%-of-snaps cameos. On paper it looks like a breakout: 8.79 yards per attempt (6th of 54) and 9.64 adjusted net yards per dropback (3rd).

The start was far narrower than the box score makes it look. Three completions of 20-plus air yards, all caught, added 9.3 EPA. Across all 46 dropbacks, sacks and scrambles included, he finished at -0.4 EPA, so those three throws carried the whole day. Underneath, his 26 throws under 10 air yards averaged 0.007 EPA a play, roughly break-even. The 10 throws behind the line were a drag at -0.39 a play. All four intermediate attempts fell incomplete. On the five red-zone plays he produced two sacks, one completion and no success. That doesn't make it a bad game. It makes it a game that would have looked very different if one of those deep balls had been broken up.

Some of it is real progress. His bad-throw rate fell from 16.5% as a rookie to 11.8%, and he hasn't thrown an interception in 34 attempts after throwing 10 in eight games last year. But 34 attempts is a hint, not a verdict, and the rookie season he is building on was poor: -0.188 EPA a play, 55th of 63. The cost of his style is still there. He holds the ball (3.09 seconds to throw), and pressure turned into a sack 38.5% of the time, 34th of 42. His 12.8% sack rate ranks 50th of 54. Last year his pressure-to-sack rate was 22.3%, 15th, so the sack problem may be partly this one game behind a line that allows the most QB hits in the league. Holding the ball is a career-long trait, though, not a fluke.

Going forward, his value depends on opportunity, not on how he played. As long as the depth chart reads QB2 and Watson is healthy, Sanders is a handcuff. If he gets another start, expect the same shape: a high ceiling from shots down the field, a low floor from sacks and an underneath game that doesn't move the ball on its own.

strengths.title: He hits the deep shot
strengths.body: All three of his 20-plus-yard attempts were completed, one for a touchdown, and they added 9.3 EPA. That was the engine of his 297-yard start. He is willing to hold the ball and let routes develop, and that patience creates these chances. The hit rate is a three-throw sample and will regress, but the willingness to take the shots is a stable part of who he is.

strengths.title: Ball security cleaned up
strengths.body: After 10 interceptions in eight rookie games, he has none in 2026, and his bad-throw rate dropped 4.7 points. It's the most encouraging development on the card, because sloppy accuracy and turnovers were what sank his rookie EPA. Thirty-four attempts can't confirm it, but the bad-throw improvement shows up in charting, not just in luck with dropped picks.

strengths.title: Spreads it to the young receivers
strengths.body: KC Concepcion (0.83 EPA a target) and Denzel Boston (nine targets, +2.9 EPA) carried his passing game, and throws to the right side produced 0.796 EPA a play with both touchdowns. He found working answers with the second-tier receivers rather than forcing everything to one target.

concerns.title: Sacks are the cost of the style
concerns.body: A 12.8% sack rate ranks 50th of 54, and pressure became a sack 38.5% of the time. He holds the ball over three seconds, and the Browns' line allows the most QB hits in the league, so the two problems feed each other. His rookie pressure-to-sack rate was far better, which suggests this one game exaggerates it. Even so, a long time to throw is who he has been, and sacks will keep capping his floor.

concerns.title: Short game doesn't move the ball
concerns.body: Outside the deep shots his passing was flat. Throws under 10 air yards averaged 0.007 EPA, screens and throws behind the line lost 0.39 a play, and four intermediate attempts all fell incomplete. His CPOE of -6.71 ranks 45th of 54, in line with his rookie -5. Without a dependable rhythm underneath, his production rides on a few big hits.

concerns.title: Backup role limits everything
concerns.body: He is QB2, and Watson reclaimed the job in Week 10 after Sanders' lone start. Without an injury or a coaching decision, his weekly floor is a handful of snaps or none. His rookie line, -0.188 EPA a play (55th of 63), is the bigger sample and the reason he isn't the starter.

trend.note: A one-snap appearance in Week 3, a 6%-of-snaps cameo in Week 8, then a full 22.7-point start in Week 9 before going back to the bench. His usage swings with the depth chart, not his form.

nextGame.headline: Soft Raiders defense, but he's probably holding a clipboard
nextGame.body:
If Sanders plays, this is the kind of defense that flatters him. Las Vegas ranks 28th in defensive EPA and pass EPA, last in success rate allowed, and last against short passes, which is exactly the area he struggled to make productive in New Orleans. The deep-ball defense (22nd) is no wall either. QBs have averaged 19.9 PPR points a game against them (29th) with 2.5 touchdowns a game. The catch is the pass rush: the Raiders rank 7th in QB hit rate, and Cleveland's line allows the most hits in the league. For a passer who holds the ball and took five sacks in his only start, that is the pressure point.

Availability is the whole story on his side. He is QB2 behind Watson, who isn't on the Browns' injury report, so the most likely outcome is little or no playing time. Cleveland comes off the bye with 14 days of rest. Fullback Michael Burton is on IR, which barely touches the passing game. For Las Vegas, edge rusher Kwity Paye (neck, 61% of snaps) is questionable and DT Thomas Booker IV (ankle) sat last week. If either misses, the Raiders' hit rate loses some teeth.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders rush vs. a leaky line
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas hits quarterbacks at the 7th-highest rate, and Cleveland allows hits more often than anyone. Combined with Sanders' 3.09-second time to throw, that is how a soft defense could still produce a lot of sacks. Paye's neck injury is the variable here.

keyMatchups.title: Short-pass defense is the worst
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders allow 0.243 EPA on short passes, last in the league. That could turn Sanders' break-even underneath game into real yardage, because easy completions would cut how long he has to hold the ball.

keyMatchups.title: WR2s feast on Las Vegas
keyMatchups.body: Second receivers have scored 4.8 PPR points a game over their averages against this defense, the most in the league, at 0.86 EPA a target. That suits a passer who got his best work from Concepcion and Boston rather than a single alpha.

nextGame.watch: Whether Watson is still the starter by Sunday. Without a change at QB, the matchup doesn't matter for Sanders.

restOfSeason.body:
As a backup, the default is close to nothing: occasional garbage-time or injury-relief snaps. The real question is what a start looks like if he gets one. Expect fewer than his Week 9 297 yards. Three-for-three on deep balls won't repeat, and without that his rookie-year efficiency profile (low CPOE, flat short game) is the better guide. A start in the 190-250 yard range is a fair expectation, with a touchdown or two and a sack rate that stays high because of how long he holds the ball and how often the Browns' line gives up hits.

The interception-free start is the piece to watch for real growth. The drop in bad throws is a skill signal, but last year's 1.25 picks a game says some interceptions will come back with more volume. The deep shots, the high sack rate and the patience in the pocket are the stable parts of his profile.
swingFactors: Watson's health and the coaching staff's patience with him
Whether the deep-ball hits keep coming without the sacks
Pass protection on a line allowing the most QB hits

confidence.note: One start and 34 attempts, in a backup role with no guaranteed snaps.
